findings.title: A confirm pass can bypass the round cap permanently
findings.claim: Termination is first-match-wins, with CONVERGED evaluated before CAP; therefore convergence at round 10 with `--confirm` starts round 11 despite rounds being defined as `1 … cap`, and if that confirm pass raises a P0/P1, later rounds can never satisfy `N = --rounds` because N is already greater than 10
findings.why: this violates the fixed ten-round cap and creates a non-terminating path
findings.fix: make CAP use `N >= --rounds`, define confirm as consuming one of the capped rounds, and schedule it only when `N < --rounds`.

findings.title: Resume has no authoritative checkpoint for a half-finished round
findings.claim: `--resume` says to enter at the next round, while an interrupted Codex call is supposed to rerun the same round; between prompt creation, Codex output, meta creation, response, fixes, verification, and commit, many combinations such as `round-N.md` without `round-N.meta` or `response-N.md` are possible, but no rule identifies the completed phase or whether existing output is safe to reuse
findings.why: a fresh Claude session can skip an uncommitted response/fix, overwrite a valid result, or start N+1 from an uncommitted N, so the promised lossless resume is not implementable
findings.fix: define an atomic per-round phase journal and a resume matrix; derive N from the last completed committed round, rerun the same N after an incomplete Codex phase with a freshly truncated output file, and otherwise resume the exact unfinished parse/respond/verify/commit phase.

findings.title: The final ledger state cannot name the single commit that contains it
findings.claim: An accepted finding must become `fixed@<hash>` before the round commit, but that commit’s hash cannot be known until after its contents—including `ledger.md`—are committed; writing the hash afterward leaves the source-of-truth ledger uncommitted or requires a second commit, while amending changes the hash again. The ruling flow has the same contradiction, and `exchange.md` is regenerated only after the purported one round commit
findings.why: the committed checkpoint cannot contain the state the next round and `--resume` are told to trust
findings.fix: replace the self-referential status with `fixed` plus a round number whose commit is located from round metadata/history, and regenerate `exchange.md` before the single commit; alternatively explicitly adopt a separate state commit and revise the one-commit rule.

findings.title: Delta prompts omit context needed to verify prose fixes
findings.claim: A fresh Codex session receives only reusable policy sections, a compact ledger, the diff, and Claude’s response; it does not receive the original finding body, the subject-identification section, or a current reading manifest, even though the cost model says delta rounds read “the manifest ranges a fix touched.” For a prose subject, diff hunks alone do not provide enough surrounding invariants to check whether the revised wording contradicts an unchanged section
findings.why: two implementations can produce materially different prompt context, and Codex may confirm a local edit without validating its document-level consequence
findings.fix: include the verbatim awaited finding blocks, current subject path and revision, and generated current ranges covering each entire changed semantic section plus cited dependency sections; add explicit template markers for mechanically extracting reusable sections.

findings.title: The parser contract does not define a closed grammar
findings.claim: Only a missing `Verdict` or missing awaited ID is declared a format violation, while behavior is unspecified for duplicate or unknown IDs, multiple/invalid verdicts, malformed finding headings, invalid prior-result words, or incompatible transitions such as `withdrawn` for a `fixed@` row and `resolved` for a `rejected` row
findings.why: an unattended parser can update the ledger differently depending on implementation or silently strand a P0/P1 in an unhandled state
findings.fix: define the complete accepted grammar and transition matrix, require exactly one valid result for every awaited ID, reject unknown/duplicate IDs and invalid status combinations, and exercise each case in parser fixtures.

findings.title: Explicit `git add` paths do not isolate round commits
findings.claim: The spec acknowledges unrelated working-tree changes but only forbids `git add -A`; `git commit` still includes unrelated entries already staged before `/refine`, and adding a subject path stages pre-existing unrelated edits within that path. For impl subjects, the argument is a diff range, so “subject paths” is itself undefined when fixes add new files
findings.why: a round can sweep user work into an autonomous commit or omit an accepted fix outside the original file list
findings.fix: snapshot index/worktree state at setup, require a clean index, reject overlap with pre-existing dirty paths, track every path modified by the loop, and commit only that exact allowlist with Git’s path-limited commit form.

findings.title: Error and metadata detection rely on an untyped transcript
findings.claim: The failure rule greps a combined stdout/stderr transcript for any line beginning `ERROR:`, so prompt content or command output quoting such a line can produce a false CODEX FAILURE. The claimed token “footer” is not actually at EOF in the prototype: `tokens used` appears before a second copy of the final response
findings.evidence: spec L253–L262; `.codex-help.txt` L102–L106; `.codex-round-1.log` L12860–L12864 and L12910–L12914
findings.why: unattended control flow and accounting cannot safely depend on arbitrary review text
findings.fix: remove stale output before every attempt, use process status plus output freshness for success, and parse a validated structured event stream or otherwise separate machine-status records from transcript text.

findings.title: `--effort low` has no defined delta effort
findings.claim: The CLI accepts `high|medium|low`, but delta rounds are merely “one step lower”; there is no tier below `low`
findings.why: implementations must either reject a documented invocation or choose different behavior
findings.fix: define the mapping explicitly, for example `high → medium`, `medium → low`, and `low → low`.

findings.title: An accepted user ruling can contest the same ID repeatedly
findings.claim: A `still open` report increments cycles to two and contests an ID, but accepting the user ruling resets cycles to zero; two more incomplete-fix reports contest the same ID again, and repeated accepts can repeat this at rounds 3, 5, 7, and 9
findings.why: the cycle limit does not provide the stated lifetime bound and the autonomous loop can repeatedly stop for rulings on one ID
findings.fix: define cycles as lifetime counters that do not reset, or close the ruled ID and create a separately bounded fix-verification ID with explicit post-ruling behavior.

findings.title: The confirm pass has no prior-decision context
findings.claim: A confirm pass is “round-1-shaped,” so it receives `brief.md` verbatim rather than the ledger or prior responses and may reintroduce a rejected, withdrawn, or user-closed issue as a new finding with a new ID
findings.why: optional confirmation can create duplicate rows and unnecessary contested stops instead of testing the final revision
findings.fix: retain the full-review scope but append a prior-decisions appendix and require genuinely new evidence before assigning a new ID to a previously decided issue.

findings.title: The cited out-of-credits fixture is not the supplied artifact
findings.claim: The testing section describes the real round-2 log tail as an out-of-credits error with empty output, but the available log contains a token count followed by a completed review, and its actual final five lines are the review’s `Not verified` section
findings.why: the promised real regression fixture cannot be constructed from the named artifact, weakening verification of the most important failure path
findings.fix: preserve an immutable minimal log/output pair from the actual failure or explicitly make this a synthetic fixture and specify the expected exit status and file state.

verified: The installed CLI supports `codex exec -o`, `-C`, `-s read-only`, a stdin prompt via `-`, and generic TOML config overrides via `-c`: `.codex-help.txt` L3–L25, L53–L70, L105–L106.
`codex exec resume <session_id> -` and `-o` on resume are valid forms: `.codex-help.txt` L117–L125, L190–L191.
The prototype successfully used the proposed initial invocation shape, and its header exposes workdir, model, sandbox, effort, and `session id:`: `run-round.sh` L34–L40; `.codex-round-1.log` L1–L10.
The prototype output matches the parser baseline of 2 P0, 8 P1, and 1 P2: `codex-round-1.md` L5–L36.
The exact Git exclusion pathspec in spec L53–L55 is accepted by Git in this worktree.
Normal convergence does not treat `fixed@` or `rejected` P0/P1 rows as closed; they remain awaited until `resolved` or `withdrawn`, and CONVERGED requires a terminal state: spec L197–L207, L294.
The reading-manifest instruction is actionable: this review used the supplied ranges without directory exploration; the escape for evidence needed by a finding is explicit at spec L117–L122.
The prototype’s measured token count supports the approximate 200k round-1 statement: `.codex-round-1.log` L12860–L12861. Section 10 correctly labels the delta figures as estimates: spec L327–L333.
not_verified: The claimed eight-minute prototype duration and 40–80k-token/2–4-minute delta estimates could not be verified: the prototype runner does not record duration (`run-round.sh` L33–L41), and no successful measured delta metadata was supplied.

Whether `medium` and `low` are accepted values for `model_reasoning_effort` is not enumerated by the help capture; only the generic `-c` mechanism and the prototype’s successful `high` value were evidenced.
The future templates and scripts do not yet exist, so reusable-section extraction, atomic writes, parser behavior, and dry-run fixture behavior could not be executed.
Per the manifest, the full ~800KB logs were not read; only the requested header/footer ranges and targeted lines required to investigate the failure-detection claims were inspected.
